title: The Unexpected Detention
premise: In the tiny town of Marrow Creek, Zephyrine Blackwood has perfected the art of being fine—until he finds coded instructions hidden in his late grandmother's recipe box, revealing she ran an underground network that protected the town's outsiders for decades. When the network's last safe house is threatened by a vindictive school board member, Zeph must rally the misfits nobody believes in, win the state baking championship as cover, and expose the truth at the graduation ceremony everyone expects him to skip. He ends the story not as the town's only out kid, but as the founder of its next refuge.
about_author: Gideon Sandoval is a former small-town debate coach who grew up as the only openly queer student in his graduating class of forty-three. He writes stories about kids who build families out of misfits and recipes.

chapters.title: Cardamom and Ciphers
chapters.summary: Zeph's POV. Sorting his grandmother's belongings after the funeral, Zeph discovers the recipe box's final card isn't a recipe at all but coordinates and a key, leading him to a hidden basement beneath the shuttered diner. The emotional beat is grief cracking open into wonder: he realizes the grandmother who taught him to survive also built a machine for it.

chapters.title: The Detention Society
chapters.summary: Zeph's POV, with interludes from Delia, the school board member hunting the network. Zeph assembles the 'Saturday Detention' kids—delinquents, burnouts, and one terrified valedictorian—to restore the safe house, while Delia maneuvers to demolish the diner before graduation. The beat is wary belonging: strangers learning to trust each other over flour and fear.

chapters.title: Everything Burns at 425 Degrees
chapters.summary: Dual POV climax. At the state baking championship, Zeph's team deliberately loses the final round to smuggle the network's ledger to the judges' stage, while Delia's demolition crew descends on the diner. Zeph must choose between loyalty to the friends who want to stay hidden and the truth that will save them. The beat is sacrifice: winning by losing, in public.

chapters.title: Graduation, Extra Frosting
chapters.summary: Zeph's POV, closing with Delia's downfall. Exposed by the ledger and the championship spectacle, Delia resigns; the town, forced to look, mostly chooses to see. Zeph reopens the diner as the Marrow Creek Youth Kitchen with his ragtag crew as staff. The beat is earned homecoming: he was never fine, and now he doesn't have to pretend.
